title.title: A hyperbolicity cone that is not spectrahedral
title.subtitle: Claim: the generalized Lax conjecture is false; an explicit cone is no linear slice of any PSD cone

plain: Optimisation methods run on a big family of cones, long believed to be slices of one standard cone. Not so

lines.note: Generalized Lax: every hyperbolicity cone is a slice of a PSD cone

beats.text: Hyperbolicity cones generalize the PSD cone, and interior-point methods run on them
The counterexample: a determinant built from the Choi–Lam biquadratic form
Its cone equals $\{L(x) \succeq 0\}$ for no linear pencil $L$ of any size

steps: Suppose some matrix pencil described the cone exactly
Rescale it and push it to rank-one limits
That yields a square the Choi–Lam form forbids: contradiction

data.assume: a PSD pencil for the cone

achievement.label: Generalized Lax conjecture (open since Helton–Vinnikov, 2007)
achievement.context: Counterexample: degree 20 in 23 variables. A second paper claims a cone with no semidefinite lift at all
achievement.note: The stronger no-lift claim (Projected Lax) is the one not in Lean

verify.detail: In Lean: the explicit degree-20 cone is not spectrahedral. Not: the no-semidefinite-lift theorem
verify.ourCheck: From the paper and its Lean docs; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Hyperbolicity cones generalize matrix cones. The counterexample is built from the Choi Lam form.
Any matrix description would yield a square that Choi Lam forbids.
Claimed: no linear slice of any size.

sources.quote: p(X,Z,y)=det((det X)Z - Phi_y(adj X)) on S^4 x S^4 x R^3 (23 variables, degree 20
built from the Choi-Lam biquadratic form
The generalized Lax conjecture (every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral) has been open since then.

sources.ref: article, Hyperbolicity cones that are not slices of the PSD cone
sources.quote: Hyperbolicity cones generalize the cone of positive semidefinite matrices, and interior-point methods run on them.
The stronger 'no semidefinite lift / not a spectrahedral shadow' theorem (paper 1, which disproves the Projected Lax Conjecture) and paper 3's lift are NOT formalized.
